senses.definition: Proceeding by small additions, each one adding a little to what is already there.
senses.caution: About how work is delivered it is praise, but about results it means the gains are small. In finance it means the extra amount above the usual baseline.
senses.example: The gains are incremental per release, and it is the compounding across two quarters that the case actually rests on.

cues.text: A committee asks how you will de-risk an eighteen-month programme, and your answer is small releases that each stand on their own.
You are describing model improvements that are real but modest, and you want the honest word for them before somebody else uses it against you.
You are explaining how you are learning a language: twenty minutes a night, nothing dramatic.
A friend asks whether the new phone is worth the upgrade, and every improvement in it is a small one.

distractors: Done all at once, with no way back.
Growing by a fixed percentage each period rather than a fixed amount.
A change that removes a feature instead of adding one, to keep the product simple.
Work that cannot be split up, because none of it is any use until all of it is done.

senses.definition: Processing only what is new or changed since the last run, not everything again.
senses.caution: Say what it is measured against, such as the last run or the last backup. An incremental job that misses a change leaves old data behind without any error.
senses.example: The nightly load is incremental, so it reads only the rows changed since midnight instead of the whole table.

cues.text: Your nightly backup copies only the files that changed since the previous backup instead of everything, and you need the adjective for that kind of backup.
A data pipeline used to reload ten years of history every night, and you rebuild it to pick up only the new rows. What adjective describes the new design?
A build tool recompiles only the files you edited rather than the whole project. You want the adjective for that kind of build.

distractors: Safe to run more than once, because a second run changes nothing the first did not.
Made from separate systems that each keep their own data but work together as one.
Created for one run and deleted as soon as that run is finished.
Spread across many servers so that one failure does not stop the work.
Run in a safe, sealed area.
